title: Relative nerve of a chain of symmetric operads is a family
statement: Use symmetric infinity-operads, inert maps, families and their inert edges as in [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family], and the explicit relative nerve $R_{[m]}(D)$ of [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation]. Let $D:[m]\to\mathsf{sSet}_{/N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)}$ be a strict diagram of small symmetric infinity-operads whose transition maps preserve inert edges and whose maps to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ commute strictly. The subset-indexed relative-nerve formula defines a family $(b,t):R_{[m]}(D)\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$ with vertex fibres exactly $D(i)$; its inert edges are precisely the inert cocartesian edges in the vertex operads. For $x\in D(a)$ and $y\in D(b)$ with $a\le b$, its mapping spaces satisfy natural equivalences $\operatorname{Map}(x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{D(b)}(D(a\to b)x,y)$ over the pointed-map base, while for $a>b$ they are empty. Every order map $\beta:[l]\to[m]$ identifies the pullback with $R_{[l]}(D\beta)$ over both bases. These assertions include repeated vertices, $m=0$, zero arity, and empty fibres.

proof.text: Use the subset-indexed formula for $R_{[m]}(D)$ from [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation], now with $C=[m]$. An $n$-simplex is an order map $\sigma:[n]\to[m]$ and compatible maps $t_J$ into the value $D(\sigma(\max J))$ for every nonempty subset $J\subseteq[n]$. Applying an order operator reindexes $\sigma$ and the subsets, so the compatibility equations are preserved. The two projections are therefore simplicial: $t$ is the projection to $N([m])=\Delta^m$, while $b$ is the pointed-map projection obtained by applying the structure map of the terminal value in each $t_J$ (the equations make this independent of $J$). On a constant $\sigma=i$, all $t_J$ are restrictions of one simplex, so the vertex fibre is exactly $D(i)$ over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$.

source.place: HTT Definition 3.2.5.2 and Remarks 3.2.5.4, 3.2.5.7; explicit subset-indexed relative-nerve formula

proof.text: Each $D(i)\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ is an inner fibration over the quasicategory $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, so every $D(i)$ is a quasicategory and the composite $[m]\to\mathsf{sSet}$ satisfies the hypothesis of [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation]. That theorem gives that $t:R_{[m]}(D)\to\Delta^m$ is a cocartesian fibration with fibres $D(i)$, that an edge over $a\le b$ is $t$-cocartesian exactly when its edge in $D(b)$ is an equivalence, and that transport along $a\le b$ is $D(a\to b)$; in particular the edge $c_x:x\to D(a\to b)x$ with $t_{\{0,1\}}$ the degenerate edge at $D(a\to b)x$ is $t$-cocartesian, and its pointed-map projection $b(c_x)$ is an identity. Let $x\in D(a)$, $y\in D(b)$, $a\le b$. Since $\Delta^m$ is the nerve of a poset, its right-pinched mapping spaces are points (for $a\le b$) or empty, and a mapping simplex between two vertices over the same $b$ projects to a constant simplex, so $\operatorname{Map}_{R}(u,y)=\operatorname{Map}_{D(b)}(u,y)$ for $u\in D(b)$. The cocartesian mapping criterion [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion] for $c_x$ and $t$ gives a homotopy pullback whose bottom row is $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^m}(b,b)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^m}(a,b)$, a map of points; hence precomposition with $c_x$ is an equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_{D(b)}(D(a\to b)x,y)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_R(x,y)$. It is natural in $y$ (postcomposition) and commutes with the maps to $\operatorname{Map}_{N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)}$ because $b(c_x)$ is an identity and all transition maps are over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. If $a>b$, a mapping simplex would project to an edge $a\to b$ of $\Delta^m$, which does not exist, so the mapping space is empty. Same-vertex mapping spaces are those of $D(i)$.

source.place: HTT Definition 3.2.5.2, Remark 3.2.5.7, Proposition 3.2.5.21; cocartesian mapping criterion

proof.text: Inner horns. Let $0<k<n$ and let a horn $\Lambda^n_k\to R_{[m]}(D)$ be given over an $n$-simplex $(\beta,\sigma)$ of $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$. The horn supplies the data $t_J$ for every nonempty $J\subseteq[n]$ except $J=[n]$ and $J=[n]\setminus\{k\}$; both missing subsets have maximum $n$ because $k<n$. The maps $D(\sigma(\max J)\to\sigma(n))t_J$ for the faces $J=[n]\setminus\{i\}$, $i\ne k$, agree on overlaps by the compatibility equations, so they form a horn $\Lambda^n_k\to D(\sigma(n))$, lying over $\beta$ because every transition map commutes strictly with the projections to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$. Since $D(\sigma(n))\to N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ is an inner fibration (the symmetric-operad convention of [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction]), it has a filler $t_{[n]}$ over $\beta$; put $t_{[n]\setminus\{k\}}=t_{[n]}|$. All equations involving the new subsets hold by construction, so $(b,t)$ is an inner fibration, and $R_{[m]}(D)$ is a quasicategory. Inert lifts. Let $x\in D(j)$ over $\langle r\rangle$ and let $\alpha:\langle r\rangle\to\langle r'\rangle$ be inert; let $e:x\to x'$ be a $p_j$-cocartesian lift in $D(j)$, which exists because $D(j)$ is a symmetric infinity-operad. We show $e$ is $(b,t)$-cocartesian using [lem-coef-infinity-cocartesian-mapping-criterion]. For $z$ over parameter $c<j$ all four corners of the criterion square are empty (the parameter coordinate of the base mapping spaces is $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^m}(j,c)=\varnothing$). For $c\ge j$, the equivalences of Step 2 identify the criterion square for $e$ at $z$, over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$, with the criterion square for $D(j\to c)e$ at $z$ in $D(c)$ over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$, since $\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^m}(j,c)$ is a point. Because the transition maps preserve inert edges, $D(j\to c)e$ is $p_c$-cocartesian, so this square is a homotopy pullback by the criterion. Hence $e$ is $(b,t)$-cocartesian over $(\alpha,\mathrm{id}_j)$, as the family definition [def-coef-symmetric-operadic-family] requires. Conversely, a family inert edge has parameter edge an equivalence of $\Delta^m$, i.e. an identity, so it lies in some $D(j)$; for $z\in D(j)$ its criterion square over $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$ is literally its $p_j$-criterion square, so it is $p_j$-cocartesian. Thus the family inert edges are precisely the inert cocartesian edges of the vertex operads. Equivalences. The equivalences of $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)\times\Delta^m$ are the pairs $(\alpha,\mathrm{id}_j)$ with $\alpha$ a bijection, which is inert. Its cocartesian lift $e:x\to x'$ is an equivalence: the horn-lifting property of the cocartesian edge $e$ for $\Lambda^2_0$ with edges $e$ and $\mathrm{id}_x$, over the base $2$-simplex $(\alpha,\alpha^{-1},\mathrm{id})$, gives $g:x'\to x$ and a $2$-simplex witnessing $ge=\mathrm{id}_x$; then $\Lambda^3_0$ with $\{0,1\}=e$, faces this $2$-simplex and the degenerate $2$-simplices $s_1e,s_0e$, over the base $3$-simplex $(\alpha,\alpha^{-1},\alpha)$, has a filler whose face $d_0$ witnesses $eg=\mathrm{id}_{x'}$ ([def-coef-infinity-fibrations]). So $(b,t)$ is an inner fibration between quasicategories lifting equivalences with given source, hence a categorical (Joyal) fibration by [lem-coef-joyal-quasicategory-characterizations](1).

source.place: HTT §3.2.5 relative-nerve horn description, together with HA Definition 2.3.2.10 and Proposition 2.3.2.11

proof.text: Fix $x$ over $(j,\langle r\rangle)$ and choose inert lifts $x\to x_i$ over $\rho_i$; by Step 3 every such lift lies in the fibre $D(j)$ and is $p_j$-cocartesian. Let $y$ lie over parameter $a$ and $\langle k\rangle$. If $a\le j$, the equivalences of Step 2 (natural in the target, compatible with the projection to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$) identify $\operatorname{Map}_R(y,x)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_R(y,x_i)$ with $\operatorname{Map}_{D(j)}(y',x)$ and $\operatorname{Map}_{D(j)}(y',x_i)$, $y'=D(a\to j)y$, while the base corners are $\operatorname{Map}_{N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)}(\langle k\rangle,-)\times\operatorname{Map}_{\Delta^m}(a,j)$ with the second factor a point. Thus the square of the family definition becomes the symmetric-operad mapping-space Segal square of $D(j)$ for $y'$ and $x$, a homotopy pullback by the product axiom in [lem-coef-operadic-approximation-restriction], and its composition homotopy is transported along the same natural equivalences. If $a>j$, the two left corners are empty (both the total and the base mapping spaces have empty parameter coordinate); for $r\ge1$ the right corners are empty too, and for $r=0$ they are points; in both cases the square is a homotopy pullback because its homotopy fibre product is empty. For $r=0$ and $a\le j$ the products are points and the Segal axiom states that the left vertical map is an equivalence onto the corresponding base component, which is again the operad axiom.

source.place: HA Definition 2.3.2.10 and Proposition 2.3.2.11; HTT §3.2.5 mapping-space description

proof.text: For an order map $\beta:[l]\to[m]$, pull back the displayed subset formula along $N(\beta)$. An $n$-simplex is then an order map $[n]\to[l]$ together with the same maps $t_J$ valued in $D(\beta(\sigma(\max J)))$, which is exactly the formula for $R_{[l]}(D\beta)$. The identifications commute with every simplicial operator and with both projections to $N(\mathrm{Fin}_*)$ and the simplex base. The pullback compatibility in [lem-cbc-strict-presentation-transport-representation] therefore gives the asserted identification over both bases.

source.place: HTT Remark 3.2.5.7 and Proposition 3.2.5.21; pullback of the relative-nerve formula

proof.text: Repeated vertices merely make some transition maps identities, and the same formula still applies. For $m=0$ the relative nerve is the single fibre $D(0)$. Empty fibres give empty vertex fibres and empty mixed mapping spaces, while zero arity gives the terminal product in the Segal square. Thus all listed edge cases are included without an extra existence or nonemptiness hypothesis.
